processing: Both a large-leaf early cultivar and its protected tea. Made mainly as green tea: bud tea, maojian and ordinary green grades, by heat fixing, shaping and drying.
harvest_season: An early-budding plant, so spring picking starts early; bud-only grades typically come from the earliest picking, as with other green teas.
appearance_dry: Plump leaf with a lustrous green colour; bud grades are stout, upright and heavily downy.
appearance_liquor: Bright, vivid green in the bud grades.
taste_profile: Rich, lasting aroma with a fresh taste and a sweet return; bud grades are smooth and brothy with a young-leaf fragrance.

brewing.notes: General settings for a Chinese green. Large leaf gives a stronger cup, so shorten the steep if it turns bitter.

vintage_note: As with other Chinese green teas, it is sold as the current spring harvest, with the bud grades at the top. Drink it within about a year. Check that it comes from Taoyuan County, since the cultivar is also grown elsewhere in Hunan.
description:
Taoyuan Da Ye is a double thing: a large-leaf early-budding tea plant from Taoyuan County in Hunan, and the protected green tea made from it. The name just means Taoyuan big leaf. It is grown most in Taoyuan, and also around Changde, Shimen, Anhua, Xinhua, Changsha and Yueyang.

The bush is a tall, semi-spreading shrub with thick, rather sparse branches and glossy yellow-green oval leaves, and it stands up well to cold and drought. The leaf is plump, and it goes into bud teas, maojian and everyday green grades.

The cup has a rich, lasting aroma and a fresh taste with a sweet return. The bud grade sold as 'Ye Cha Wang' has stout, silver-tipped buds and a bright green, smooth liquor. Big leaf can run stronger than small-leaf greens, so watch the steep time.

Buy by grade and by picking date. 'Wild tea king' is a trade name for bud tea, not evidence of wild plants, despite how it sounds.
history:
The cultivar was developed from 1976 to 1992 by the Taoyuan County tea seedling station and the tea institute of Hunan Agricultural University. Two brands, Gudongchun and Lingya, gained national pollution-free product certification in 2003 and 2004.

In October 2005 Taoyuan Da Ye tea received national protection of origin.
